## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

DataLayerCapabilitySource — core-sync/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/sync/link/WearableLinkStateSource.kt

## Trigger

Collecting `WearableLinkStateSource.observeNodeConnected()`, which calls
`localNodeId()` — observed (reached from `PlatformModule` and
`SyncModule`'s construction of `LinkStateMonitor`, on every application
launch after the first).

## Today

`DataLayerCapabilitySource.localNodeId()` calls
`capabilityClient.addLocalCapability(CAPABILITY_NAME).await()` and lets
its `Task` failure propagate as a thrown exception — the class comment
(`:50-55`) states this is deliberate, modelled on `reachableNodeIds()`'s
own unhandled `Task` failure. `addLocalCapability` persists the
(package, capability) registration in Play Services across launches, so
every launch after the first receives `DUPLICATE_CAPABILITY` and the
thrown exception reaches `observeNodeConnected()`'s `Flow`, uncaught,
killing the application. `addListener` and `removeListener` (`:75-85`)
each discard the `Task` `CapabilityClient.addListener` /
`removeListener` return, so a registration failure there is invisible
as well. Nothing in `CapabilitySource` or `DataLayerCapabilitySource`
declares a failure type for the link boundary: no test exercises a
second call to `localNodeId()`.

## Expected

`localNodeId()` treats `DUPLICATE_CAPABILITY` as the normal outcome of
a second registration and completes without throwing; every other
`ApiException` — device not paired, service unavailable, outdated
Play Services version — is caught and turned into a declared
"link absent" outcome instead of an unhandled exception, consistent
with the pattern `ExerciseSessionSystemImpl` already applies by reading
`ExerciseTrackedStatus` before each attempt. The class comment at
`:53-55` that documents the thrown-exception behaviour as intentional
is removed together with the code it justifies. `addListener` and
`removeListener` no longer discard the `Task` `CapabilityClient`
returns: their failure is observed and handled the same way, not left
silent. A test covers a second call to `localNodeId()` and asserts it
does not throw.
